As the years go on, a mild displeasure brews within the god: These lands, they were a gift. A harsh world, to grow the strength of its inhabitants. Why are they so ignored?

So Umbralocht waited. Perhaps he would place a boon upon the first arrival.

And, in time, there was a first arrival! How joyous. How glorious.

Yet by and by, as Umbralocht gathered his winds to greet the newcomer, the newcomer was gone. So swiftly perished?

A time of thought followed. How did such a newcomer appear so deeply in the Heaviness, avoiding Umbralocht's awareness all the while? How, why so swiftly gone?

It transpired, that at this time, that one of the Fleshchanged Flora disappeared. Umbralocht does not look in closely at his creations, lest they be discovered and their purpose foiled; But this is a time of beginnings, and so the winds whisper across them, time to time, to marvel at their progress. Whether they live, or die, or save, or devour, or fail, or succeed, the winds chortle their approval. And one was suddenly gone.

The timing was inescapably suspicious. These happenings must have been related.

No sorcery would yet allow such a thing. No artifice of mortals. No beast, and no godly treasure. It must have been, therefore, an effort of the gods themselves.

That the gods should pluck at and toy with his followers in this way made Umbralocht uneasy. If any god should quietly cleanse their population of this infestation by hand, it would deny their purpose.

The winds gathered, and Umbralocht considered his allies. He would seek remedy. Quickly, quickly, before this got out of hand, he would seek counsel and assistance.
